summary: When two people shechted a korban Pesach for the same person, whose korban does he eat from? This mishnah teaches about a wife, an orphan, and a servant.

chunks.en: A woman, while she lives in her husband's house,
chunks.st: A woman, when she is living in her husband’s house,

chunks.he: שָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ בַּעְלָהּ וְשָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ אָבִיהָ,
chunks.en: if her husband shechted for her and her father shechted for her,
chunks.st: if her husband slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf and her father also slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf,

chunks.en: she should eat from her husband's.
chunks.explain: We assume she wants to be in her husband's group.
chunks.st: she should eat from her husband’s lamb
chunks.stMore: because it is assumed that the wife intended to be included in her husband’s group.

chunks.he: הָלְכָה רֶגֶל רִאשׁוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ,
chunks.en: If she went on the first Yom Tov to spend it in her father's house,
chunks.st: However, if, as was often customary, she went on the first Festival following her marriage to observe the Festival in her father’s house,

words.note: The first Yom Tov after her wedding.

chunks.he: שָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ אָבִיהָ וְשָׁחַט עָלֶיהָ בַּעְלָהּ,
chunks.en: and her father shechted for her and her husband shechted for her,
chunks.st: then, if both her husband slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf and her father also slaughtered the Paschal lamb on her behalf,

chunks.en: she may eat in the place she wants.
chunks.st: she may eat in whichever place she wishes,
chunks.stMore: since it is not obvious with whose group she intended to be included.

chunks.en: An orphan whose guardians shechted for him,
chunks.st: In the case of an orphan with multiple guardians, if each of his guardians [apotropsin] slaughtered a Paschal lamb on his behalf, intending that he be included in their group,

words.note: Grown-ups who take care of an orphan.

chunks.en: may eat in the place he wants.
chunks.st: he may eat in whichever place he wishes.

chunks.en: A servant of two partners
chunks.st: A slave jointly owned by two partners

chunks.en: may not eat from either of theirs.
chunks.explain: Unless they agreed first whose korban he will eat from.
chunks.st: may not eat from the lamb of either of them,
chunks.stMore: unless it was stipulated beforehand from whose lamb he will partake.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶן חוֹרִין,
chunks.en: One who is half a servant and half free,
chunks.st: One who is half slave and half free man

chunks.en: may not eat from his master's.
chunks.st: may not eat from his master’s lamb.
chunks.stMore: It is assumed that the master did not intend to allow this person’s free half to partake of the lamb, and therefore the master did not slaughter the lamb with him in mind. Consequently, the half slave is not included among those registered for his master’s offering unless he was explicitly included.

summary: A master sent his servant to shecht his korban Pesach. This mishnah teaches what happens if the servant forgot which animal the master asked for.

chunks.en: One who says to his servant,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his slave:

chunks.en: "Go and shecht the korban Pesach for me,"
chunks.st: Go and slaughter the Paschal offering on my behalf,
chunks.stMore: but does not specify which type of animal to slaughter, the halakha is as follows:

chunks.en: if he shechted a young goat,
chunks.st: If the slave slaughtered a kid,

chunks.en: he may eat it. If he shechted a lamb,
chunks.st: his master may eat it; if he slaughtered a lamb,

chunks.en: he may eat it. If he shechted a young goat and a lamb,
chunks.st: his master may eat it. If the slave slaughtered both a kid and a lamb,

chunks.en: he eats from the first one.
chunks.st: his master should eat from the first one that was slaughtered;
chunks.stMore: the second is invalid and should be burned.

chunks.en: If he forgot what his master told him,
chunks.st: If the master had stated explicitly which type of animal to slaughter, but the slave forgot what his master said to him,

chunks.en: what should he do?
chunks.st: what should he do?

chunks.en: He should shecht a lamb and a young goat and say,
chunks.st: He should slaughter both a lamb and a kid and say the following stipulation:

chunks.en: "If my master told me a young goat,
chunks.st: If my master said to me that I should slaughter a kid,

chunks.en: the young goat is his and the lamb is mine.
chunks.st: the kid is for his Paschal offering and the lamb is for mine;

chunks.en: And if my master told me a lamb,
chunks.st: and if my master said to me that I should slaughter a lamb,

chunks.en: the lamb is his and the young goat is mine."
chunks.st: the lamb is for his Paschal offering and the kid is for mine.
chunks.stMore: In this way, once the master ultimately clarifies what he had originally said, both animals may be used accordingly.

chunks.en: If his master forgot what he told him,
chunks.st: If his master also forgot what he said to him, neither animal may be used, since it has not been clarified which of the animals the slave and master are registered for.

chunks.en: both of them go out to the place of burning,
chunks.explain: Nobody knows whose korban each one is.
chunks.st: Therefore, both of them, the lamb and the kid, go out to the place designated for burning, in accordance with the halakha pertaining to offerings that may not be eaten.

chunks.en: and they do not need to bring a korban on Pesach Sheni.
chunks.st: However, despite this, both the master and slave are exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ if the blood of the animals has already been applied to the altar before the master forgot.

summary: A father promised the korban Pesach to whichever son reached Yerushalayim first. This mishnah also teaches until when people may join or leave a korban Pesach.

chunks.en: One who says to his sons,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to his children:

chunks.en: "I am shechting the korban Pesach for
chunks.st: I am slaughtering the Paschal lamb on behalf of

chunks.en: whichever of you goes up first to Yerushalayim,"
chunks.st: whomever of you goes up first to Jerusalem,

chunks.en: once the first one brought in his head and most of his body,
chunks.st: as soon as the first of the children has entered his head and the majority of his body into Jerusalem,

chunks.he: זָכָה בְחֶלְקוֹ וּמְזַכֶּה אֶת אֶחָיו עִמּוֹ.
chunks.en: he gets his share and gets shares for his brothers with him.
chunks.explain: The father really wanted all of them to be in the group.
chunks.st: he has acquired his portion and acquires on behalf of his brothers their portions together with him.

chunks.en: People can always sign up for it, as long as there is
chunks.st: Additional people can always be registered for a Paschal lamb, as long as there will be

chunks.en: a kezayis of it for each and every one.
chunks.st: at least an olive-bulk of the lamb’s meat for each and every person registered.

chunks.en: People may sign up and pull out
chunks.st: People can be registered and withdraw themselves from being registered for a Paschal lamb

chunks.en: from it until it is shechted.
chunks.st: until it is slaughtered.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: until he throws its blood.
chunks.st: Even until the priest sprinkles the blood.

summary: Someone in a korban Pesach group added another person to his share. This mishnah teaches what the rest of the group may do.

chunks.en: One who signs up other people with him in his share,
chunks.st: If one who is registered for a Paschal lamb unilaterally registers another person with him in his portion of the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: the members of the group may give
chunks.st: the other members of his group are permitted to give him,

chunks.en: him his own share,
chunks.st: i.e., the one who included the additional person, only his portion, which was originally allotted to him.

chunks.en: and he eats from his,
chunks.st: And he, the additional person, eats from his portion, i.e., the portion of he who added him;

chunks.en: and they eat from theirs.
chunks.explain: They did not agree to add the new person.
chunks.st: and they, the other members of the group, eat from theirs.
chunks.stMore: This is because they did not agree to the inclusion of the additional person.

summary: People who had a kind of tumah and are becoming tahor: this mishnah teaches on which day a korban Pesach may already be shechted for them.

chunks.en: A zav who had it happen twice
chunks.explain: He must count seven clean days and go to the mikvah.
chunks.st: A zav, a man who experiences a gonorrheal discharge, who saw two sightings of discharge is ritually impure.
chunks.stMore: To become ritually pure and able to partake of offerings, he must wait seven clean days during which he does not see any discharge. Then he immerses in a ritual bath. He will then be considered ritually pure upon nightfall.

words.note: Someone with a kind of tumah.

chunks.en: we shecht for him on his seventh day.
chunks.explain: By night he will be tahor and can eat it.
chunks.st: One slaughters the Paschal lamb on his behalf if Passover eve is on his seventh day, despite the fact he is still not ritually pure at the time of slaughter, since by the night of Passover he will be ritually pure and able to eat it.

chunks.en: If he had it three times,
chunks.st: If he saw three sightings, in which case, in addition to the seven clean days he must bring an offering on the eighth day to be allowed to partake of offerings,

chunks.en: we shecht for him on his eighth day.
chunks.explain: On that day he brings his korban and becomes fully tahor.
chunks.st: one slaughters the Paschal lamb on his behalf if Passover eve is on his eighth day.
chunks.stMore: It is presumed that by the evening his offering will have been brought and his purification complete.

chunks.en: A woman who waits one day for one day,
chunks.st: A woman who keeps watch a day for a day
chunks.stMore: is one who became ritually impure after experiencing a discharge of blood outside of her regular menstrual cycle on one day or two consecutive days. She must keep watch on the day following her last discharge to be certain she does not experience any additional discharges. To ritually purify herself, she should, on that day, immerse in a ritual bath, and on condition that she doesn’t experience any discharges throughout that day, she is considered ritually pure already from the time she immersed.

words.note: A woman with a kind of tumah who must wait one day.

chunks.en: we shecht for her on her second day.
chunks.st: If she saw a discharge on one day, one slaughters the Paschal lamb on her behalf after she has immersed on her second day, despite the possibility that she may see additional discharges later that day.

chunks.en: If it happened two days,
chunks.st: If she saw a discharge on two days,

chunks.en: we shecht for her on the third day.
chunks.st: one slaughters the Paschal lamb on her behalf on the third day.

chunks.en: And a zavah, we shecht for her on the eighth day.
chunks.st: And a zava is a woman who experienced discharges on three consecutive days. She must, like a zav, wait a full seven clean days with no discharges, immerse, and then bring a sacrifice on the eighth day. One slaughters a Paschal lamb on her behalf only on the eighth day.

words.note: A woman with a kind of tumah.

summary: We may shecht a korban Pesach for people who might not be able to eat it, but only together with others. This mishnah teaches who they are.

chunks.en: An onen, and one digging through a pile of fallen stones,
chunks.explain: Someone might be under the pile.
chunks.st: An acute mourner, i.e., a mourner on the day of the death of an immediate relative; and one clearing a pile of stones that collapsed on top of a person, in which case there is a possibility that the person buried underneath is dead and his corpse will impart ritual impurity to the person clearing the pile;

words.note: A mourner on the day a close relative died.

chunks.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁהִבְטִיחוּהוּ לְהוֹצִיאוֹ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים,
chunks.en: and so too one who was promised to be let out of prison,
chunks.st: and similarly, one whom the governing body promised to release from prison on the night of Passover;

chunks.he: וְהַחוֹלֶה וְהַזָּקֵן שֶׁהֵן יְכוֹלִין לֶאֱכֹל כַּזַּיִת,
chunks.en: and a sick person and an old person who can eat a kezayis,
chunks.st: and an ill person and an elderly person who are still capable of eating an olive-bulk of meat,

chunks.en: we shecht for them.
chunks.st: one slaughters the Paschal lamb on their behalf,
chunks.stMore: since they are currently fit to eat the Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: But for all of them we do not shecht
chunks.st: However, with regard to all of them, this is only true when they are included in a group with other people who will definitely be able to partake of the lamb; but we do not slaughter the Paschal lamb

chunks.en: for them alone,
chunks.st: on their behalf if they are by themselves, either as individuals or in a group composed entirely of such people,

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא יָבִיאוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח לִידֵי פְסוּל.
chunks.en: in case they cause the korban Pesach to become unfit.
chunks.st: because perhaps they will cause the Paschal lamb to become disqualified,
chunks.stMore: since there is a possibility that by the night of Passover they will be unable to partake of the Paschal lamb.

chunks.en: So if something happened that made them unfit,
chunks.st: Therefore, since they were registered for a Paschal lamb and it was slaughtered when they were still fit to partake of it, even if a disqualification occurred to them later, preventing them from partaking of the Paschal lamb,

chunks.en: they do not need to bring Pesach Sheni,
chunks.explain: The korban was shechted for them when they were fit.
chunks.st: they are nevertheless exempt from observing the second Pesaḥ.
chunks.stMore: The exemption from the second Pesaḥ is dependent not on whether they partook of a Paschal lamb, but on whether it was validly slaughtered on their behalf.

chunks.en: except for the one digging through the pile,
chunks.explain: If the person under it had died.
chunks.st: This holds true except for one who was clearing a pile of stones where the person buried underneath was eventually found dead,

chunks.en: because he was tamei from the start.
chunks.st: because in such a case the person searching for him certainly stood over the corpse at some point. He had therefore become ritually impure from the outset, even before the Paschal lamb was slaughtered.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, he would not have been fit even during the slaughter and will have to observe the second Pesaḥ.

summary: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei argue whether a korban Pesach may be shechted for one person alone. The mishnah also teaches which groups may not be made.

chunks.he: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד,
chunks.en: We do not shecht the korban Pesach for one person alone.
chunks.st: We do not slaughter the Paschal lamb on behalf of an individual, only for a group of people;

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yosei allows it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei permits it.

chunks.en: Even a group of a hundred
chunks.st: And even if there is a group of one hundred

chunks.en: who can't eat a kezayis,
chunks.st: who together are unable to eat an olive-bulk of it,

chunks.en: we do not shecht for them.
chunks.st: we do not slaughter on their behalf.

chunks.he: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין חֲבוּרַת נָשִׁים וַעֲבָדִים וּקְטַנִּים:
chunks.en: And we do not make a group of women, servants and children.
chunks.st: And we do not make a group for a Paschal lamb that consists of women, slaves, and minors.

summary: This mishnah teaches when an onen, and a ger who joined the Jewish people on Erev Pesach, may eat the korban Pesach.

chunks.he: אוֹנֵן טוֹבֵל וְאוֹכֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לָעֶרֶב,
chunks.en: An onen goes to the mikvah and eats his korban Pesach at night,
chunks.explain: The Rabbis made an onen's mourning last into the night too, but not for the korban Pesach.
chunks.st: An acute mourner, i.e., a mourner on the day of the death of an immediate relative, is prohibited from eating sacrificial food. By Torah law, the prohibition applies only to the day of death itself, but it is permitted to partake of sacrificial food on the following night. By rabbinic decree, the period of acute mourning is extended to include the night as well. Despite this, an acute mourner immerses and eats his Paschal lamb in the evening.

chunks.en: but not other korbanos.
chunks.st: But he may still not eat other sacrificial food.

chunks.en: One who hears about the death of his relative,
chunks.explain: He heard about it more than thirty days later.
chunks.st: However, one who hears about the death of his dead, i.e., he discovers that one of his immediate relatives died more than thirty days after the death, his status of acute mourning applies on a rabbinic level.

chunks.en: and one who gathers bones for himself,
chunks.explain: Moving his parents' bones to their lasting kever.
chunks.st: And one who gathers the bones of his parents, who are buried in a temporary location for their flesh to decay and who is moving them to a permanent burial place must also observe a day of acute mourning by rabbinic decree.

chunks.en: goes to the mikvah and eats korbanos.
chunks.st: These mourners immerse and eat all types of sacrificial food at night.
chunks.stMore: Since in these cases, even during the day, the mourning is by rabbinic decree, the Sages did not extend it into the evening.

chunks.en: A ger who became a Jew on Erev Pesach,
chunks.st: With regard to a convert who converted on Passover eve,

words.note: Someone who joins the Jewish people.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he goes to the mikvah and eats his korban Pesach at night.
chunks.st: He immerses and eats his Paschal lamb in the evening.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.he: הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הָעָרְלָה כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַקָּבֶר:
chunks.en: one who leaves the state of not having a bris is like one who leaves a grave.
chunks.explain: He must wait seven days to become tahor, like someone who became tamei from a dead person.
chunks.st: One who separates from the foreskin by being circumcised is ritually impure, like one who separates from the grave after coming in contact with a corpse.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, he must first observe the seven-day purification process necessary to remove ritually impurity imparted by a corpse. Only then, from the eighth day onward, may he partake of sacrificial meat.
